findings.title: Classification treats test-support code as project source, which can admit unfair cases
findings.description:
- D11 defines project source as a file under the tree, not under `.venv`, and not `test_*.py`, `*_test.py` or `conftest.py`.
- Helper modules in a test directory, such as `tests/helpers.py`, `tests/fixtures/*.py` or `tests/utils/`, therefore count as project source.
- An exception raised there classifies as `project_exception`, and an `ImportError` naming such a module classifies as `missing_symbol`.
- The first is read as a project crash that a fix cures, which qualifies a hidden test. The second sends a test through the wrong branch of the test-first check.
- The architecture says that where a check cannot decide, the case is "excluded, never admitted". This definition fails open for any project with test helpers.
- Fix: exclude files under the project's test directories (or any path component named `tests`/`test`) from project source. Alternatively, send exceptions from non-source support code to `other_exception`. Add a fixture for the helper-module case.

findings.title: Cleanup after a partial `BenchmarkSandbox.__enter__` failure is unspecified
findings.description:
- `__enter__` creates the lock, the tree, the scrubbed home with carryover symlinks and the output directory, then installs. Step 4 (install) and step 3 (home seeding) can fail.
- Python does not call `__exit__` when `__enter__` raises. The design says all four paths are removed on exit unless `keep()` was called, and names the orphan sweep only for dead owners.
- A failed install in the same live process (a likely case for stale locks, which the architecture says will lower yield) would leave `<id>.home` with symlinks to the user's real auth file and a partial `.venv` until the next sweep. It would also leave a lock.
- Verification step 5 only asserts "no `.venv` created".
- State that `__enter__` cleans up on any failure and re-raises, and add a test for it.
- Also specify what happens when a granted profile's carryover file does not exist, for example `openai-oauth` with no `.codex/auth.json`. Fail at grant time with a named error rather than leaving a dangling symlink for the probe to trip on.

findings.title: Design is heavier than the slice must deliver
findings.description:
Cuts and deferrals, none of which is plan-assigned scope:
- **`registry.py` with `adapter_for`.** It has one entry and a "no detection step" (D9). Have the CLI and callers construct `PythonBenchmarkAdapter` directly. Add the registry with the second adapter (Future Work 1).
- **"Carryover replaced" symlink verification** (D8, last bullet). It is a second probe-time mechanism for a hypothetical rename-write. Fold it into the PM-facing DEVLOG answer: after one probe, run `ls -l`. Add automated detection only if a provider turns out to rotate tokens.
- **`SCRUB_SPEC_VERSION` and `scrub_spec_version` in the identity digest** (D6). No consumer exists until 422/424. Declare it where qualification records need it, or keep it but drop the "incremented whenever rules change" process until then.
- **`pytest_reporter/` mock `_patch` introspection** (D10). It exists for one `FailureKind` edge, is tied to Python 3.13 internals, and reaches for the `self` frame of mock. Consider classifying a patch-target AttributeError raised inside `unittest/mock.py` as `missing_symbol` from the exception message and frame module instead. D11 already puts anything unmatched into the exclude-by-default bucket.
- **`sq benchmark sandbox --node` and `--suite` plus `--keep` path printing.** These are verification tools, but a single command with a pytest selection would meet the walkthrough. Fold the unused surface into the 422 consumer.
- **Seeding the home with three config files plus a fixed git identity** is required. The `HARNESS_TOOL_ALLOWLIST` indirection with symlinks is justified only for `git` and `uv`, so keep it small.

Every one of these is defensible alone, but together they make a 12-decision slice rated 3/5. The auth spike (step 1) is the only part the plan marks as risk-first.

findings.title: `reference_sha` and `other_exception` extend the architecture
findings.description:
- Both extensions are reasoned and acceptable. The architecture's identity list omits `reference_sha`, and the plan lists three failure kinds where D11 has five.
- 422 and the architecture should adopt both so the fairness rule's wording matches. In particular, `other_exception` reduces yield by excluding call-site `TypeError`s that the architecture's wording would arguably admit as "exception raised by project code".

findings.title: Carried auth files are symlinks to the user's real tokens
findings.description:
- Symlinking means model-written code in a producer run can read, overwrite or delete the user's real `~/.codex/auth.json` or `.claude/.credentials.json`.
- The Risk section covers token rotation but not producer-caused corruption.
- This sits at the same trust level as P6 today and under #213's remit, so it is not a blocker. It is worth one line in "Limits of the scrub" so 424 can decide whether to copy instead.
